correctness.rationale: In the one-sided zero-indexed word, padding the offset to k bits adds only the possible 11 across the join, so aligned blocks are signed P_k for even m and signed Q_k for odd m. The concatenation recurrences give the stated p,q,U,V by induction, also maintaining nonnegative prefixes via V_k≤p_k. The split at half the block gives the stated bounds for a+b and a−b. For k≥2 the P-then-Q bound is strictly below H_k. In the Q-then-P case the maximizing offsets require aligned signs at even k and opposite signs at odd k, with both nonzero contributions at equality. The first matching signed block pairs are m=1 and 11 for even k, m=3 and 5 for odd k, by direct signs of m and m+1. Their smallest offsets are (2L+1)/3 and (L+1)/3 respectively, coming from the least prefix maxima and lying strictly below L. This proves the global first starts suggested by the finite checks. An independent exact replay for 2≤k≤15 computed all signed adjacent-block types and their first block indices, enumerated every offset per type, and reproduced both extrema and first indices. This checks finite cases, not a replacement for the infinite proof. The prior-recurrence derivation below also confirms the formulas.

evidence: For all n≥1 the first paper gives M(4n)=2M(n)+2, sign symmetry of the extrema, and position-sensitive recurrences for Σ_r. The second provides synchronized prefix sums and exact shell extrema with locations and shift formulas. Its published min_rss/max_rss predicates operate on prefix-sum shells, not first starts of window extrema.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The dyadic heights are prior: use M(1)=1 and M(2)=2 in the fourfold recurrence. The stronger per-start identities, not the statement of the heights alone, give all first starts by equality and order. The prefix automaton is not itself a published least-start automaton, and generic automata closure is not needed for the failure.

evidence: For even n let g(i)=εΣ_r(i,n), ε=±1, with maximum H; use the analogous g_4 for length 4n. Lemma 4(1)–(3) gives g_4(4i+s)≤2H for s=0,1,2. Lemma 4(4) and the displayed relation r(4i+3)=−(−1)^i r(i) give g_4(4i+3)=2g(i+1)+(−1)^i[g(i+1)−g(i)]. For odd i this is g(i+1)+g(i)≤2H. For even i it equals 2H+2 precisely when g(i+1)=H and g(i+1)−g(i)=2, since adjacent window sums differ by 0 or ±2.

If the first start b attaining H is odd then b−1 is even, g(b−1)<H, and the necessary jump is exactly +2. Thus the first scaled start is 4b−1: it attains equality and no earlier qualifying index can have i+1≥b. The small anchors at n=4 are (b_+,b_−)=(7,47), and at n=8 (27,43), obtained by scanning only through the first attainment of the known heights. They are odd and oddness is preserved. Solving b(4n)=4b(n)−1 from these anchors yields exactly all four claimed formulas.

Independently for L=4^h, Theorems 9 and 11 give a maximum difference H at n=(5L−2)/3 for s(n+L)−s(n); for n<L the shift bounds and previous shell minimum/initial values give strictly less than H, and for L≤n<(5L−2)/3 the only pair at distance L that attains both shell extrema is the displayed one. The start i=0 is also excluded by the preceding shell bound. Hence i=(5L+1)/3 is already a consequence of the prior prefix-sum identities.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For every dyadic class the only candidate attaining the known scaled maximum is the earliest old extremizer followed through the same residue rule. The two fixed anchor lengths and affine iteration are routine substitutions, not a new structural step demarcating the first occurrence. This covers the full stated first-location result and is stronger evidence than merely being able to recover it by general automata computation.
searches: arXiv:1606.06935 §3.2 Lemma 4(1)–(4), proof of Lemma 4, and Lemma 5; §3.1 Theorem 1

evidence: Σ_r(i,2^k) is exactly the target window sum without changing its start convention. For inclusive prefix sums s and i≥1, T_k(i)=s(i+2^k−1)−s(i−1). Least maximizing/minimizing starts are the same as least prefix lengths containing an extremal factor, after adding the fixed window length.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An Abelian-complexity spectrum does not remember where a value occurs. Lemma 4 of the cited paper is stronger than that spectrum: it supplies identities at each start i in all four residue classes. The prefix-sum reformulation gives an independent overlapping derivation for the even-positive case.

The prior shell locations are not a table of all four sliding-window first starts, but the paired minimum and maximum separated by L give the even-positive attaining window and, with Theorem 11, give its first occurrence. originality.rationale: The first-start formulas are mathematically correct but all four follow as a direct equality case of the already published fourfold sliding-window recurrence (Lü–Chen–Wen–Wu, Lemma 4(1)–(4)), together with their known extrema and two small anchor lengths. This is specific position-sensitive coverage, not an inference from the complexity spectrum alone or from mere computability. Separately, published prefix-extremum and shift identities already imply the even-positive branch. No source was found printing the identical four-formula display apart from the same Resultary record; the failure is mechanical corollary coverage, not a claim that the display appeared verbatim.
residual_risks: The full Lü–Han paper was not accessible via the attempted route. An earlier explicit statement of all four locations could exist, but no such statement is required for the demonstrated corollary coverage.

value.rationale: Shortest prefixes containing extremal factors are a natural observable, but the claimed closed forms are obtained by the direct equality case of the published per-position recurrence and two fixed tiny anchors. The self-contained block proof may be expository, but the finding does not contain a separate non-mechanical exact result to credit: it neither classifies a wider family of first locations nor delivers a different structural theorem as its claim.
